cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Database observability is measuring signals that show whether a database is healthy and where it is heading: p95 and p99 query latency, connection and pool usage, replication lag, lock waits and deadlocks, disk and IOPS, and the slow query log.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Alert well before hard limits. Track growth trends for capacity planning and know your levers: bigger instance, replicas, pooling, partitioning. Load-test before big events. Schedule maintenance like vacuum and analyze, and plan upgrades with a tested rollback path.

questions.q: Average latency is 20 ms. Is the database fine?
questions.a: Not necessarily. Averages hide the tail; 2 percent of queries at 800 ms hurt pages that run many queries.
Deferring maintenance silently degrades query plans over time.
Before a known traffic event, not after it causes an incident.
